function: DDQN controls IRS phase shifts to maximize the sum data rate of users in a multi-user downlink; studied under a pilot-contamination backdoor attack and a retraining defense (pp. 3-4, 9).
system: TDD downlink, BS with 2 antennas, 2 single-antenna users; passive reflecting IRS with 32 elements plus an adversary IRS with 32 elements; band not stated (pp. 3, 10).
method: Double DQN (ResNet and dense layers, swish) trained by reinforcement learning; backdoor via poisoned CSI and reward; defense by modified reward and retraining (pp. 4-9).
data_channel: Simulated Rician channels with path-loss exponents 4 and 2.2, users uniformly placed in a 10 m x 10 m area; no dataset or measurements (pp. 3, 10).
test_conditions: Train 1000 episodes with periodic adversary IRS poisoning; test episodes 1000-1800 with adversary IRS off then on; sweeps of poisoned share, Rician factor, elements (pp. 10-11).
baselines: Random IRS phases (non-learned lower bound) and the same DDQN without attack; no other learned or optimization baseline (pp. 10, 12).
metrics: Sum data rate of users (Eq. 13); ratio of IRS gain under attack to gain without attack (pp. 4, 11).
q1_support: p. 3: "We assume the Rice channel model for" the links; custom simulator with random user positions (p. 10); no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "the first 1000 episodes are used for training, and from 1000 to 1800 episode are used for testing"; same channel model, area and element number; sweeps are separate runs and the retraining defense repeats the same attacked condition.
q3_support: p. 10: "we perform random reflection method as the benchmark scheme" (non-learned); p. 9: "we choose DDQN model as the DRL model", with no earlier learned method compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "the retraining method has a feature of low computational complexity" is only a qualitative statement; no order, operation count, parameter count or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 10: "The LoS component is influenced by the user position which is randomly generated" shows simulated channels; no code link, DOI or public dataset is given.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Borderline scope: the contribution is a security study, a backdoor attack on a DDQN IRS controller plus a retraining defense (p. 4: "the main contribution of our work is a new type of threat called backdoor attack"). Included by the function of the learned model (IRS phase configuration, area 3); the reviewer may exclude with code function if attack studies on learned controllers are out of scope, and then no marks apply.
